architecture.authority: gba.provider_verification_configs: per connection, version by trigger, one active, opaque store:name secret_ref (secret-like refused), one-way revocation, no config for a revoked connection
architecture.routing: gba.provider_receipt_routes: ingress_id -> tenant_id, connection_id; one per connection; immutable; SELECT policy only for gba_receipt_writer; runtime has no access
architecture.provisioning: database owner only, inside explicit company context; runtime and writer may only revoke a config; no new role, no definer-rights function
architecture.entry_point: receive_routed_receipt(pool, ingress_id, raw, signature, key_store=...) replaces the caller-supplied ReceiptVerifierBinding; only route/config/binding are read before the K1a signature check
architecture.attestation: composite FK (tenant, connection, verification_config_id) -> configs plus an insert trigger under FOR SHARE: missing, foreign or revoked config refused
architecture.upgrade: explicit refusal when K1c attestations exist, under a temporary owner policy dropped in the same transaction
architecture.guard: schema guard covers 6 tables, policies by role name, the partial unique index and per-group privileges of gba_runtime and gba_receipt_writer
architecture.not_admission: connections stay not_admitted and test-mode only; no HTTP route, provider account/key, worker or money
